reader.requirement: READ ... INTO does the READ, then (only if it was successful) moves the current record, sized by the RECORD clause, from the record area to identifier-1 by MOVE without CORRESPONDING, as a group move when the FD has RECORD IS VARYING; identifier-1's subscripts are evaluated after the read; the record stays in the record area.

edition-consulted.switches: IntoPhraseRules cite text: §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR8b for 1985 versus §2023:14.9.30.4 GR4 b)
ctx.Edition.DialectLevel selects only the cite phrase; sender choice (BoundCurrentRecord, group move for FORMAT 2 VARYING) is edition-invariant

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the arm is shared; the 1985 text's group-move sentence is the behaviour 2023 states through GR16 sizing
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is one case; probes cover VARYING, unsuccessful read, subscripts

probes.printed: READ INTO G (14 bytes) of a 3-byte then 10-byte record: G=[ABC           ] then [0123456789    ] (space padded, group move); record at EOF leaves G unchanged ([yyyy...])
probes.expected: group move pads; no move on unsuccessful READ

probes.printed: VARYING record '12' INTO PIC 9(4): N=[12  ] (group move, alphanumeric); fixed 9(2) INTO PIC 9(4): M=[0012] (numeric move)
probes.expected: group move only when RECORD IS VARYING

probes.printed: READ F INTO T(RI), RI read from the record (3): T(3)=[3abc], R=3abc; at EOF no move
probes.expected: subscript evaluated after the read; record kept in the record area

probes.printed: READ after EOF without FILE STATUS: abnormal termination status 46
probes.expected: read past end is an error, outside this rule

citations.check: cite.py --check with 'If the file description entry contains a RECORD IS VARYING clause, the implied move is a group move.' returned the rule text (a. ... b.)

reader.notes: Only sequential files probed; keyed READ INTO (VIII.4.5.4, IX.4.5.4) share BindIntoPhrase by code reading, not probed. RECORD clause sizing for a CONTAINS-larger record is handled by RecordClauseExceedsDescriptions, not probed.

refuter.evidence: cite.py --check '§1985:VII.4.4.4 GR8' 'The current record is moved from the record area to the area specified by identifier-1' returned OK. Keyed READ INTO (the untested path): k1 indexed READ F INTO G KEY IS K gave G=[BBB22222    ] R=[BBB22222] (move, record kept, space padded to 12); keyed READ with INVALID KEY (ZZZ) left G=[yyyyyyyyyyyy] (no move on unsuccessful read). k2 relative READ F INTO G with RECORD CONTAINS 4 TO 8 gave G=[abcdef      ] (group move sized by the record read). RECORD larger than descriptions: k4 FD RECORD CONTAINS 10 with 01 R PIC X(4), file written as 10 bytes through a second FD, READ F INTO G gave G=[abcdefghij  ] R=[abcd], so the move is sized by the RECORD clause (10), not by the 4-byte description. k3 same FD written through the 4-byte record gave G=[abcd        ] (consistent). One side observation outside this rule: READ F NEXT after an unsuccessful keyed READ ended with status 46 in k1; the text for that position effect is outside GR8 and was not adjudicated.
